# A fresh controlled comparison of A2 (D586): provenance check and design, version 2 (council round 95), nothing sent

## 1. Provenance: no stored topic set is held out

| Stored topics | Used in developing arms A to A3 |
|---|---|
| July (three runs, about 40 topics) | the probes' motivating, recovery, refusal and disputed topics; PROMPT-AUDIT-LINE-2 §7 recount; DECLINE-AUDIT read all 66 descriptions and outcomes |
| fortnight (13 topics) | the probes' motivating, regression and harm-control topics; CENSUS.md |
| week of 10-06 (13 topics) | the probes; CENSUS.md; d436-reading |
| week of 09-22 (7 questions) | PROMPT-AUDIT-LINE-2 (the line-2 failures that started the line) |
| carried library (10-06 articles) | the same week's matters as above |
| Alex's 44 (Stage A) | the ladder step's own design; D426: not tuned further |

**Conclusion:** fresh topics need the first step to open them from articles no new-system run has read.

**Exposure, rechecked today** (`fresh-exposure-2026-11-16/`; the census re-run into a new folder, through every stored file):
- **The week of 2026-10-13..19:** 383 eligible articles; 20 sent before by a run, probe or reading packet. The census list is
  `week-10-13-exposure.txt`.
- **The other 363:** they appear only in source-page work (page fetching and lineage diagnostics). The earlier census excluded that
  work by rule, and so does this one.
- **Per day:** 48, 66, 73, 52, 44, 46, 54.

## 2. Design (version 2)

- **The run:** clean Step 1 as frozen (c8, D427), on the whole week in source order, all 383 articles.
  - The 20 seen-before articles stay in the run, so the library meets what it would meet.
  - Topics they open are out of the population, as in the 10-06 week.
- **Why the whole week:** from a carried library fewer topics open than from empty. The carried-library test opened 4 against 16 on
  the same 11 articles. The 10-06 week opened 13 topics from 272 articles from empty, so three days would likely give fewer than 5.
- **Starting library:** the completed library of the week of 10-06 (`poc/data/clean-second-week-2026-11-15/week-continued/c1`).
  - It is real earlier material (D559). It is not a library accumulated over several weeks: that week began from empty and was
    finished after a stall (`second-week/COMPLETION-DESIGN.md`). This is stated with every number.
  - The entry point and starting state are proven at $0 first, as for the carried library.
- **Cost and limits:**
  - The 10-06 week charged $3.55 for 272 articles, $1.11 of it on cut attempts. That is about $0.0094 an article clean and $0.013 with
    losses, so $3.6 to $5.0 for 383.
  - A new ledger with a ceiling of $5.00. A dry run checks the per-article reservations, retries and the library's size before the
    send.
  - The answer-choice calls are about $0.10. Reader sessions sit outside the ledger and their dollar cost is not priced.
  - The D439 spend after the run would be about $31.6 of $40.
- **The answer-choice step:** each topic in the population gets the frozen request (control) and A2, three sends each, the same day.
- **The population, classed before any answer is read:**
  - **Who:** a fresh blind Codex reader and I, separately. Each gets every opened topic and the development matters (the 66 stored
    topics' descriptions and outcomes, and Alex's 44).
  - **What:** each topic is marked as on a development matter, on a different matter, or uncertain. Where the two of us disagree, the
    topic is uncertain.
  - **The decision runs on two populations and must agree on both:** (a) every topic outside the seen-before articles; (b) its
    different-matter topics. When they disagree, the result is inconclusive.
  - Fewer than 5 topics in (a) is "not measured". The control arm is still reported as a fresh gate-1 reading of the frozen step.
- **The reading:** the unchanged gate-1 form (Alex's six lines; `clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/ladder/stage-a-reader-brief.md`), with H
  added and reported, never a veto. Two families, third readers of both, and three planted controls.
- **The expected effect on the reader (D391):** the product shows "Not judged" parts beside an answer (D570). A part left unlisted
  means the card hides what the answer ignored. A2 should make the card honest about its scope. It is not expected to change the
  judged answer.

## 3. What is reported, and the decision written now

**The unchanged gate report, for each arm:**
- all six lines under their unchanged accounting, with every failing send listed;
- unresolved points counted for the answer, then against it;
- no claim that a zero-fault line passed unless it has no failing send.

**The comparison (a diagnostic, beside the gate report):**
- **Lead** needs all of these, in both populations and both countings:
  1. A2 fails L (a part left unlisted) on fewer topics than the control, and on at most 1.
  2. A2's sends failing N (an unjustified refusal) are no more than the control's.
  3. On every other line and mark, A2's failing sends exceed the control's by no more than the spread the unchanged request showed
     against itself on that mark (`control-vs-control.txt`, sends). That bar is exploratory, and every failing send is listed whatever
     it says.
- **Inconclusive:** the control fails L on fewer than 2 topics, or the populations or countings disagree.
- **Otherwise negative.**

H is printed per topic. A lead is evidence on one fresh week. It is not a pass of Alex's gate.

# One more week through the new system, read for its answer choices: result (D550 to D553; under D439), 2026-11-15

**Label: continued, answer-choice diagnostic only.** The run stalled once and was continued as a second part; only the topics
and the answer choices were run; the matching and the judge were not. It passes no gate and reverses nothing (design, section
6). One week, one run.

## The answer

**Not clean, on both counts of topics and whichever way the open points are counted.** The step that writes answer choices
declined 9 of 39 attempts on 4 of the week's 13 topics, two of them in all three attempts, and three of the registered
zero-fault lines are missed on faults both reader families agree on. The fresh week's picture (no refusal in 21 attempts) did
not repeat.

One concrete picture: an article says the five largest cloud companies plan to spend about $800 billion in 2026 and about
$1.3 trillion in 2027. The first step opened one topic for both years. The answer-choice step declined it three times out of
three ("two yearly figures, neither named as the main one"), so in this diagnostic no answer-choice question was written for the cloud
companies' spending. The fresh week, where the first step had opened the same matter for one year, got its question in all
three attempts.

| Change between the parts | each call now waits at most 600 seconds on a silent connection (D552; `clean-arch/step1/live.py`); no request or answer is changed by it |
| Second part | the remaining 152 articles from the library after article 120, the cut call sent again (a new sample), limits reduced to what the first part left (177 calls, 25,200 seconds); 8 attempts lost on a poor network and to a second sleep, each sent again; the bound worked: the run went on by itself after waking |

# The small comparison of D559: the same 11 articles read from a kept library and from empty (D561), 2026-11-16

**Answer: on these 11 selected articles, the read with last week's library re-opened none of the four questions it already
held and filed the identified facts under them; it opened 4 questions where the read from empty opened 16, none of them on a
matter the library held (both reader families). It opened three of the four missing matters the empty read opened (not the
equity-investment commitments), so by the rule written before the run the result sits between "supports going on" and
"fails", and is reported as it is. One draw; nothing about final answers.**

Run: `poc/data/clean-carried-library-2026-11-16/` (22 of 22 reads complete, one call each, no resend; ledger $0.427 of $1.00).
Design and proofs: `DESIGN.md`, `proofs/`. My own read stored before the readers': `OWN-READ.md`. Readers (two families,
blind to which read had the library in so far as the packet allows: the library shown is part of a read): `brief-readers.md`,
`codex-readers.jsonl`, `claude-readers.jsonl`; tally `tally_readers.py` → `tally-readers.txt`.

## The rule written before the run

| Line | Result |
|---|---|
| Re-opens a held question in two or more of the four same-question cases | **0 of 4** (supply commitments, Hugging Face, Rubin's ramp, 2026 spending) |
| Drops the matter's statements where the empty read kept them, in two or more | **0 of 4** by my own reading before the readers (`OWN-READ.md`): 1, 1, 2, 1 statements filed under the held question against 1, 1, 2, 1 kept by the empty read; the readers judged the homes, not a fact-by-fact comparison. Article 15's sentence holds both $800bn for 2026 and $1.3tn for 2027; it went under the 2026 question, and 2027 is tracked by neither read |
| Opens two or fewer of the absent cases the empty read opens | opens **3 of the empty read's 4** (Groq's rack, the B200 price, Reflection AI; not the equity commitments), plus memory prices, which the empty read did not open |
| Supports going on only if, besides the two lines above, the absent cases open as in the empty read | **not met** (3 of 4); not failed either: between the two, reported as it is |

## What the readers say (both families unless split)

| | Empty | Carried |
|---|---|---|
| Questions opened | 16 | 4 |
| Of them, on a matter the library shown already held | 0 (no library) | **0** |
| Worth holding | 12 yes; 3 yes/unsure; 1 yes/no (global AI spending as a share of U.S. GDP) | 1 yes; 3 yes/unsure (memory prices, Groq's rack, the B200 price) |
| Statements filed under a held question | n/a | 27: right 17, wrong 2, unsure 2, split 6 |
| Reader-listed entries of a matter deserving a question that the read neither opened nor held (both families' lists added per article and read; names not merged, so not distinct matters) | 25 | 18 |

**The two homes both families call wrong:** customers' share of NVIDIA's receivables filed under the credit-support total
(article 173); the CFO's 70% growth outlook filed under supply commitments (article 206; D508's readers had counted the same
kind of statement as bearing on that question, so the line is disputed across readings).

**What the carried read lost:** a question on a DOJ or FTC action against the Groq deal (opened from empty; the stored October
run did not open it either; one family names it missing for the carried read, the other did not mark its worth above
"unsure"). The equity-investment commitments were not opened; their facts went under the held credit-support question, whose
own outcome reads "versus the equity investments it has made", and both families call those four homes right: the held
question's scope carries into the filing, and the separate equity-commitments question the empty read opened was not opened.

**A gap the readers name in both conditions:** questions on the company's own numbers. The Claude-family reader names the
$108bn quarterly outlook, the 70% growth outlook for fiscal 2028 and the gross-margin outlook cut to 72-73% on several
articles; the Codex-family reader names gross margins and memory costs, 2028 growth, customer concentration and the funding
of investments and payouts. These are missing questions, not missing facts: the figures were mostly kept, and in the carried
read the $108bn outlook was filed under the China question. It is the standing product rule (D382, D384) and the item Alex
ruled on (D505: such figures should reach the judgements of related questions), not something this test changes.

## Limits

Everything above is one read of these articles from a fixed library, not behaviour over a changing library. One draw; 11 articles chosen because they opened topics (not a sample of the week); a seven-topic library one week old,
itself opened from empty; the step's read of each article from a fixed library (no carry-over between articles); no
matching, answer choices or judging run. The empty reads differ from the stored October run of the same articles (12 and 35
opened nothing; 15 opened a 2026-only question): run-to-run variation, one draw each.

**No-go on v2 as written.** The revised design is clearer about the library and exposure, but its decision rule still leaves two important cases undefined.

- **The different-matter population has no minimum size.** Population (a) must have at least five topics, but population (b) could have only two. If both control topics fail L and A2 fixes one, the rule could call that a lead on the supposedly more independent subset. Set a minimum and an exercise condition for **each** population; report the rest without a verdict when either is too small. [Fresh comparison design](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/FRESH-A2-DESIGN.md>)

- **The control spread is not yet a defined bar for this population.** The saved comparison reports separate spreads by mark, group and treatment of unresolved points on the earlier 18 topics. V2 does not say which group’s spread applies to a new topic, how an absent mark is handled, or how the different population size affects the comparison. One observed difference is an exploratory reference, not an estimated error bound. Define the mapping before building and report every mark and send regardless of the bar. [Control comparison](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/control-vs-control.txt>)

The unchanged accounting also uses **35 of 44** and **28 of 44** for line 5. On a different-sized population, show the raw counts and label that original threshold as not applicable to this comparison; do not call its result Alex’s gate verdict. [Accounting](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_a/accounting.py:191>)

The exposure output supports the reported counts within its searched scope. Say “searched `poc/data`, `clean-arch` and `docs/research`, with stated exclusions,” rather than “every stored file.” The proposed $5 ceiling is at the high end of the estimate, so the $0 proof should also show what an incomplete run reports if reservations stop it; reader costs remain unpriced. [Exposure census](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/fresh-exposure-2026-11-16/exposure-census.json>)

CONSENSUS: no, because the independent subset can produce a lead with too few topics, and the prior control spread is not yet defined for this comparison.
